who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), executor, host round 2 piece front (blaze-front onto read-addressed blaze-keyed), port-memo-1113
where: crates/blaze-keyed/src/record.rs `write_traced` (`out.push_slice(payload)` after the reads and facts); crates/blaze-format/src/lib.rs `HEADER_LEN` = 56, `header` refuses a buffer not at a 16-aligned address
what: A Traced record's payload lands at 56 + 64 * (reads + facts), always 8 mod 16, so a blaze-format buffer nested in it (a surface's sections, its image) cannot open in place; blaze-front wrote its own Traced writer to pad it, and moving onto `record::write_read` loses that.
cost: an hour of reading blaze-format's writer to find why the surface's sections would not open; the surface task now refuses its own record until record.rs pads
cause: write_traced pads each slice to its element's alignment (1 for bytes), not to the alignment a nested record needs; nothing says a payload may hold a record
class: a container format that does not promise the alignment its contents need to be read in place (rule outputs-are-records: read in place)
prevention: every Traced payload starts at blaze_format::ALIGN, and a test opens a nested record in a payload
workaround: none: crates/blaze-front/src/surface.rs checks its own record and refuses with UNALIGNED
fix: record.rs write_traced: pad `out.bytes` to `blaze_format::ALIGN` before `push_slice(payload)` (listed in the front lane's report)
